explanation: Hydrogen is about half as dense as helium and once lifted giant airships. Party balloons use helium instead because, unlike hydrogen, it cannot catch fire.

claims.text: Hydrogen gas has a density of about 0.09 g per litre at 0 °C and normal atmospheric pressure.
Helium gas has a density of about 0.18 g per litre at 0 °C and normal atmospheric pressure.
Hydrogen gas is about half as dense as helium gas.
Hydrogen was used to lift large airships.
Helium does not burn, while hydrogen is highly flammable.
